to consumers; capped at 2,500 SF Marijuana Delivery Operator: authorizes the permit holder to take possession from retail stores and microbusinesses and deliver them only in person to consumers Marijuana Transporter: authorizes the permit holder to take possession from cultivation facilities, processing facilities, retail stores, microbusinesses, and other transporters; no direct interaction with consumers. 9 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC License Caps Tier V Cultivation Licenses: Capped at 5 before January 1, 2028 Microbusiness Licenses: 100 reserved for industrial hemp processors/growers, qualifying impact licensees, and USDAqualified farmers before May 1, 2027 At least 55 additional Licenses must be issued by July 1, 2027 Cultivation/Processing licenses for industrial hemp growers or processors: Capped at 20, with no more than 10 cultivation licenses and no more than 10 processing, by May 1, 2027 10 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Part II: What Localities Cannot Do 11 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Virginia Code § 4.1-629(A): State Preemption “No county, city or town shall, except as provided in §4.1-630, adopt any ordinance or resolution that regulates or prohibits the cultivation, processing, possession, sale, distribution, handling, transportation, consumption, use, advertising, or dispensing of marijuana or marijuana products.” 12 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Localities may NOT: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 Ban or “opt out” of the cannabis marketplace Impose moratoriums on cannabis business operations Regulate advertising of cannabis or cannabis products Regulate possession limits, product types, potency, or packaging Cap the number of licenses within their boundaries Increase the VCCA Board’s minimum distance/buffer requirements Impose any tax other than the 13.5% local tax 13 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Part III: What Localities Must Do 14 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Local Cannabis Tax Decisions [§ 4.1-1004(B)(1)] • Local cannabis tax rate may not be less than 1% and may not be more than 3.5% • The effective date of any such ordinance is the first day of the second month following the ordinance enactment • Once set, the rate must stay in place for three years 15 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Deadline for Locality Action: No fixed statutory deadline, but must be in place prior to the start of retail cannabis sales on July 1, 2027 Tax Revenue Tax Rate $1M in Retail Sales 1% $10,000 2% $20,000 3.5% $35,000 16 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Local Cannabis Tax Actions 1 2 3 4 Notify the VCCA within 30 days (§ 4.11004(B)(1)) Notify retail cannabis stores and microbusinesses in the locality within 30 days (§ 4.1-1004(B)(1)) Publish notice of the proposed tax (§ 58.13007) Hold a public hearing before enacting/increasing the local tax (§ 58.13007) 17 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Local Cannabis Tax for Towns Note: County tax rates do NOT apply within the limits of any town located therein Towns must independently levy their own local cannabis tax Towns that fail to act will have no local tax revenue from cannabis sales occurring within the corporate limits 18 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Adopt Internal Administrative Procedures [§§ 4.1-1000(G), 4.1-810] Localities will receive communications from the VCCA related to preliminary approvals of licenses by the VCCA in their locality Localities should adopt procedures for receiving and responding to such communications Failure to file a formal objection to any such notification within 30 days automatically waives the locality’s objection to the approval Recommend designation of locality staff for monitoring of CCA communications and drafting a form objection letter for future use Deadline for Locality Action: none, but the sooner the better 19 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Part IV: What Localities May Do 20 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Review Code Conflicts [§ 4.1-629(D) Localities should review their local ordinances to confirm there are no conflicts or inconsistencies with the new state law governing cannabis Identify conflicting local provisions that need repeal or amendment to comply with the new state law Deadline for Locality Action: Start this process with staff; referral to the Planning Commission 21 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Zoning, Land Use, & Business Licenses [§ 4.1-629(C)] Localities retain substantial authority regarding zoning, land use, and business-license requirements, subject to the limitations and preemption provisions of the VCCA. Localities should review and update their local zoning ordinances to provide regulation of cannabis businesses Zoning and land use regulation represent a significant tool for localities to regulate cannabis-related uses in their borders VCCA may deny final licenses if the establishment violates zoning (§ 4.1-1000(H)(3)) 22 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Local Zoning Tools/Options Designating zoning districts for specific cannabis-related uses Requiring conditional use permits or special exceptions – with potential risk Site plan requirements Setback and buffer distances – which may be decreased but not increased from VCCA Board minimums, which are TBD Deadline for Locality Action: Should be in place by May 1, 2027, or sooner 23 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Public Consumption Ordinances Permitted § 4.1-629(B)(1) LOCALITIES MAY ADOPT ORDINANCES PROHIBITING THE ACTS DESCRIBED IN § 4.1-1108 (PUBLIC CONSUMPTION) AND § 4.1-1109 (POSSESSION/CONSUMPTION ON PUBLIC SCHOOL GROUNDS) IN LOCAL PUBLIC PARKS, PLAYGROUNDS, STREETS, OR SIDEWALKS ADJACENT TO ANY PUBLIC STREET LOCAL ORDINANCE MAY PRESCRIBE PENALTY FOR VIOLATIONS, BUT PROVIDES NO MAXIMUM OR MINIMUM PENALTY Deadline for Locality Action: Q4 2026 to Q1 2027 24 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Buffer Reductions Allowed [§ 4.1-629(B)(2)] • Authorizes localities to adopt ordinances decreasing the VCCA Boardpromulgated minimum distance requirements: • Between Retail Marijuana Stores and Microbusinesses; or • Between a Retail Marijuana Store/Microbusiness and any hospital, public, private or parochial school or institution of higher learning, or child day program 25 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Buffer Distances, con’t Localities may only decrease buffers; they cannot impose stricter distance requirements than those set by the VCCA Board Localities should consider running a GIS suitability analysis (reviewing location of schools, day cares, parks, etc.) before adopting or stacking buffers Overlapping setbacks can unintentionally eliminate all feasible sites in the locality Deadline for Locality Action: Q4 2026 to Q1 2027 26 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Establish Hours of Sale [§ 4.1-630] 01 02 03 Authorizes cities, towns, and counties of unincorporated areas to adopt ordinances fixing the hours during which cannabis may be sold in the locality Provides any such ordinance shall provide for fine and penalties enforced as a Class 1 misdemeanor, with the right of appeal under § 16.1-106 Once passed, the clerk of the governing body must certify the ordinance and transmit it to the VCCA Board Deadline for Locality Action: Q4 2026 to Q1 2027 27 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Regulate Hemp/Tobacco Retail Locations [§ 15.2-912.4] Authorizes localities to adopt ordinances regulating the retail sale locations of retail tobacco products or hemp products intended for smoking Localities may prohibit a retail sale location on property within 1,000 linear feet of a child day center or public, private, or parochial schools Deadline for Locality Action: Q4 2026 to Q1 2027 28 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Part V: Risk Areas 29 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC De Facto Bans Overly restrictive zoning, buffers, or use-permit denials may be challenged as a de facto ban inconsistent with the statewide marketplace The most defensible ordinances generally: • Identify districts where cannabis uses are permitted • Maintain objective approval criteria • Use traditional zoning standards • Create a record demonstrating reasonable accommodation or licensed cannabis businesses 30 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC By Right vs. SUP and the De Facto Ban Issue • Requiring a special or conditional use permit carries its own preemption risk under § 4.1-629(A) and CAN BECOME A DE FACTO BAN if denials rest on generalized opposition rather than objective planning and safety findings • Objective site development requirements (lighting, screening, security, parking, etc.) generally present lower preemption risk than subjective use-permit denials 31 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC License Objection Process [§ 4.1-810] Upon preliminary license approval, VCCA notifies locality; locality has 30 days to object Objections might include: Failure to object waive local challenge 32 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC •Zoning noncompliance •Land Use violations •Local Ordinance conflicts •Factual errors Litigation Risks De Facto Bans: The locality does not expressly prohibit cannabis use, but it leaves no realistic path to operate within the locality Arbitrary and Capricious Denials: Denials based on generalized concerns about cannabis, or public opposition, rather than objective land use impacts Equal Treatment Claims: Cannabis businesses treated differently than comparable commercial uses without reasonable land use justification 33 | ©2026 Objective Site Standards Operational Conditions Repeated Permit Denials Administrative Procedures 34 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Regs That Effectively Prohibit Licensing Part VI: Departmental Checklists taxes from cannabis businesses Update business license application forms and review procedures for cannabis-specific operations Coordinate with VCCA on tax-rate notices and collection processes 36 | Impaired driving detection and enforcement protocols • Security and crime prevention planning for cash-heavy licensed retail businesses • Evidence handling and chain of custody procedures • Coordination with the VCCA on enforcement investigations • Training and policy updates reflecting the changes to the Virginia law This Photo by Unknown Author is licensed under CC BY-NC-ND 37 | ©2026 local retailers within 30 days of the local tax ordinance enactment (§ 4.1-1004) • Track incoming correspondence from the VCCA • Calendar the 30-day objection deadlines for all license applications provided preliminary approval by the VCCA (§ 4.11000(G)) • Designate recipient; create routing protocol; establish legal review timeline; create objection template 38 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC title: Notice of Special Called Meeting of the Planning Commission to discuss proposed revisions to the Comprehensive Plan and Zoning Ordinance related to solar facilities.
text: COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT botetourtva.gov 57 S. Center Drive Daleville, VA 24083 P: (540) 928-2080 F: (540) 473-2018 NOTICE BOTETOURT COUNTY PLANNING COMMISSION The Botetourt County Planning Commission will hold a work session on Monday, December 07, 2026, at 4:00 PM at 57 S. Center Drive, Daleville VA 24083 to discuss proposed revisions to the Comprehensive Plan and the Zoning Ordinance related to solar facilities. While no public hearing or comment period will be held during the work session, the public is welcome to attend. The regular session will follow at 6:00 PM. During the regular 6:00pm session, a public hearing will be held on the following items: Blue Ridge District: Botetourt County Board of Supervisors requests a Rezoning from the Agricultural (A1) Use District to the Business (B-1) Use District with possible proffered conditions as well as a Special Exception Permit for “smaller minimum district sizes in accordance with section 25-224”. The purpose of this project is to expand the existing parking lot and to add outdoor seating for the Blue Ridge branch library. This property totals 2.17 acres, is located at 28 Avery Row, and is identified on Tax Maps as parcel 112-4C. Fincastle District: Calderon Montalvan and Claudia E. Martinez Aguirre request a Special Exception Permit for a Special Events Facility in the Agricultural (A-1) Use District, with possible conditions, in accordance with Sec. 25-73. The primary purpose of this request is to bring the existing library facility into full zoning compliance with the County Code and to accommodate necessary site improvements. The A-1 use district permits a maximum of 15% impervious surface coverage. The property's existing coverage of approximately 32% already exceeds this threshold, making it nonconforming with the current ordinance. In addition to this non-conformity, the library use itself is not a permitted use within the A-1 use district. A public library is, however, listed as a permitted use under the B-1 use district. Rezoning to B-1 would resolve both nonconformities: the district's 60% maximum impervious surface allowance comfortably accommodates the existing coverage, and the use itself would become fully compliant. The proposed rezoning would also support several site improvements. The existing storage shed would be relocated from the north side of the property to the east side, eliminating a current setback non-conformity while creating space for additional parking. The project would add approximately ten (10) new parking spaces to meet growing visitor demand, along with a new concrete pad to provide expanded outdoor seating for patrons. These improvements would increase impervious surface coverage from approximately 32% to 34.5% - a modest increase that remains well within the 60% maximum allowed under B-1 zoning. Reclassifying the parcel to B-1 will resolve the property's existing non-conformities and allow the library to continue serving, and improve access for, the citizens of Botetourt County. The request applies to a 21.459-acre parcel (Tax Map Section 101, Parcel 38), adjacent to Roanoke Road (US Route 220) and College Drive (SR Route 656) containing the "Wellington Multi-Family Community" development. Page 16 of 26 Page 17 of 26 Page 18 of 26 SEP NARRATIVE On behalf of WEBT Holdings, LLC (Owner/Applicant), we are providing the narrative below as supplemental information to support the attached application for a Special Exception Permit (SEP). This request will apply to Tax Parcel 101-38, consisting of 21.459 acres, to allow for additional density for proposed multi-family dwellings on the property. Project Narrative WEBT Holdings, LLC is the Owner of the subject property. The property currently contains a mix of zoning districts including A-1 (Agricultural District), R-2 (Low-Medium Density Residential District), R-3 (Medium Density Residential District), and B-1 (Business District). This property is also located within the Gateway Crossing Overlay District and the Community Business Subdistrict, which essentially overrides the base zoning districts due to additional specific development standards. This request is for a Special Exception Permit to allow for increased density for multi-family development within this Overlay District. The maximum allowable by-right density is 8 units per acre. The Overlay District allows the maximum density to be increased to 26 units per acre with a Special Exception Permit. The proposed maximum density for this SEP request is 14.5 units per acre. Existing Conditions The property fronts on Roanoke Road, Route 220, to the east, and College Drive, Route 658, to the north. There is an existing cemetery located to the south. The remaining adjacent property to the south and west is zoned Agricultural. There is an existing creek crossing the property near the western boundary, which is not within the portion of the property that is being developed. This project is currently under construction. The approved plans include construction of 2 mixed-use buildings located along Route 220 on the eastern portion of the property, as well as 4 multi-family buildings and a pool building further back from Route 220. The plans also include other necessary improvements to support the proposed buildings, such as parking and utility extensions. Planned Improvements The proposed improvements are shown on the previously approved construction plans for “Wellington Multi-Family Community” and will remain largely unchanged as a result of this request. The 2 proposed buildings located at the front of the property are proposed to be revised from mixed-use buildings to multi-family buildings only. The commercial space originally planned for the 1st floor will be revised to additional multi-family space. This will consist of 18 additional multi-family units on the 1st floor of Building 1. The 1st floor of Building 2 will be revised to consist of 10 additional multi-family units as well as amenity/common areas for all residents of the community to use. These common areas (noted as Clubhouse area on the Architectural plans) are expected to include Fitness Center, Mail Room, Recreation Area, and Kitchen and Sitting Areas, as well as Office Space that will be used for management of the property. Preliminary architectural floor plans are included for Buildings 1 and 2 as part of this SEP application (Exhibits B, C, and D). Re-imagining these 1st floor spaces for multi-family uses rather than commercial space will allow for the Wellington Multi-Family Community to be more consistent and cohesive throughout the development and will preserve a much more tight-knit residential feel within the community. The removal of the commercial space will also have significant advantages to the Site Design for this project. Required parking on the site is reduced by approximately 100 spaces, which allows for a significant increase in landscape areas on the site. The updated parking is primarily located on the southern side of the site which allows for the development to provide additional separation from the southern property line closest to the cemetery. The large retaining wall that was planned for this area will be significantly reduced or eliminated completely. Page 19 of 26 An updated Zoning Plan is included with the application as EX-A, dated September 30, 2026, showing the updated and reduced parking areas. The by-right maximum density of multi-family units in this part of the Overlay District is 8 units/acre. It should be noted that multi-family units located within mixed-use buildings do not count toward this maximum density. Therefore, under the currently approved plan, the units on the upper floors of Buildings 1 and 2 did not count toward this density requirement. Removal of the commercial spaces will result in all units now counting toward the maximum density, which results in the need for this SEP request to increase the maximum density to 14.5 units/acre. It is important to note that only 28 additional units are being added to the project as a part of this revision. The currently approved plan includes 276 apartment units as well as +/-39,000 s.f. of commercial space. The proposed plan replaces the commercial space with 28 additional units for a total of 304 apartment units on the property. Stormwater Management The approved development includes two stormwater management facilities to serve the project. There is an above-ground detention facility located at the southwest corner of the development and an underground detention facility located at the northeast corner of the development. The current request will result in a decrease in the overall development footprint and impervious area due to the decrease in required parking and, therefore, will reduce overall stormwater impacts. Access and Traffic A new right-in, right-out entrance from Route 220 has been approved by VDOT as part of the site plan review process for this development. This entrance will include new right turn lane improvements and will have adequate sight distance and spacing from other existing entrances and crossovers. The current request will result in an overall decrease in the amount of traffic generated by the development, which will be a benefit to the Route 220 corridor and the surrounding road network. This decrease is created by the elimination of the commercial space within Buildings 1 and 2. Public Facilities This development will be served by public water and sewer. The approved plans include extension of public water and sewer mains into the property to serve the new buildings. The proposed water and sewer extensions will remain unchanged as a result of this request. However, it should be noted that the proposed residential units are anticipated to result in less water and sewer demand than the currently approved commercial space. The request is anticipated to have little or no impact to other public services, including schools, parks/recreation, and fire/rescue. Comprehensive Plan and Gateway Crossing Area Plan This property is designated for Mixed Use Neighborhood Commercial development on the Botetourt County Future Land Use Map in the Envision 2045 Comprehensive Plan. The Mixed Use Neighborhood Commercial future land use specifies “a range of commercial uses” and indicates that “associated residential development should include higher density housing types such as apartments or townhouses.” The proposed SEP request and multi-family use is consistent with the Mixed Use Neighborhood Commercial designation, particularly when taken in context with the surrounding Mixed Use Neighborhood Commercial land. There is already a significant amount of existing commercial development along this section of the Route 220 corridor, including directly to the north, to the south, and on the opposite side of Route 220 from this project. The proposed multi-family project is in a central location to complement and support these existing commercial establishments. Page 20 of 26 This project also furthers the goals of the Comprehensive Plan in other ways. The development is providing pedestrian accommodations throughout the development and across the frontage of the property, which is a characteristic of the Mixed Use Neighborhood Commercial land use. In addition to this, the project has a “walkable and compact character” and contributes to the “mix of densities and intensity of uses” within the larger overall context of the area. In addition to its consistency with the Future Land Use Map, the proposed SEP request is also in conformance with many of the Goals, Objectives, and Policies outlined in Botetourt County’s Envision 2045 Comprehensive Plan, some of which are outlined below. Development Goals: • “Reduce or restrict multiple access points off major travel routes to preserve capacity of road networks.” • “Construct pedestrian accommodations along U.S. Route 220 to connect existing residential and commercial uses.” The proposed request condenses access to one entrance, which furthers the Development Goals of the Comprehensive Plan and is consistent with VDOT Access Management initiatives. The proposed entrance is centrally located to maximize separation from existing entrances and crossovers. Goal/Objective: • “Secure and preserve woodlands, waterways, and natural assets to ensure easy access to outdoor recreation and the high quality of life synonymous with Botetourt County. In the same breath, we strive to balance preservation with necessary growth to create communities that are integrated into the natural environment, not separate.” The project concentrates the development towards the front of the property near Route 220 and preserves the area in and around the existing creek located at the rear of the site. The developed area is compact and utilizes the available property efficiently. Summary The proposed request is consistent with the Future Land Use Maps in the Botetourt County Comprehensive Plan. This project will allow for the development of much-needed housing along an important and growing corridor. The project will allow this property to be enhanced with new buildings, parking areas, landscaping improvements, and a vibrant residential community that will complement the surrounding commercial corridor. The proposed development will also provide additional housing options in an important area of the County, which is of utmost importance due to the current shortage of housing in our region. As outlined in this narrative and supporting documentation, the proposed request represents a minor change from the existing plan that is already approved and under construction. This SEP will reduce impacts to the overall transportation network, existing public utilities, and other services. The proposed SEP request will allow this property to be developed as a consistent and cohesive new community that will provide an attractive residential option for current and future residents of Botetourt County. December 1, 2026 IDENTIFICATION AND LOCATIONAL INFORMATION Request: Pattern Book Review for Depot at Fighting Creek Existing Zoning: Village Center-Planned Development (VC-PD) Parcel Size: 9.76 acres Parcel Tax Map: 26B1-1-10 Applicant: Brady Deal, Main Street Homes Owner: MFR Fighting Creek LLC Property Location: 4011 Old Buckingham Road Electoral District: District 4 2021 Future Land Use Plan: Gateway Business 1|Page 13 III. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY Project Description The applicant requests Pattern Book approval for the residential portion of a mixed-use development consisting of ten for-rent, triplex townhome dwellings. The Depot at Fighting Creek is located south of Anderson Highway along Old Buckingham Road west of Mann Road. The property is zoned VC-PD and is designated Gateway Business in the County’s Future Land Use Plan. Figure 1: Site Location Project Location The residential buildings will be oriented with their primary entrances and front façades facing internal streets. Each residential building is proposed to contain two 1,323-square-foot units and one 1,376square-foot unit, for a total of 4,022 square feet per building. The middle unit will have three bedrooms and the two side units will have two bedrooms. This request is associated with the approved rezoning case 21-01-REZ (Ordinance O-2021-04). Proffered Condition #2, Project Layout and Building Design, states: Figure 2: Site Layout “The project layout (general location of buildings, uses, and open space) and the exterior facades of buildings (architectural design and materials) within the development shall generally reflect the following exhibits.” The referenced exhibits include Exhibit #3 – “Residential Units,” dated January 7, 2021, which establishes the intended architectural character and design of the residential buildings within the development. (See Figure 3). Staff initially recommended approval of the Pattern Book application at the October 6, 2026, Planning Commission meeting, but suggested deferral after questions arose regarding whether the initial submittal “generally” reflected the proffered conditions. Concerns were identified regarding whether the proposed designs adequately reflected the intent of Proffered Condition #2 and the referenced residential exhibit. The Planning Commission voted to defer the application until the November 4, 2026, meeting. The application was subsequently deferred to the December 1, 2026, meeting to allow for revisions to the Pattern Book and further consideration of the proposed residential designs. 2|Page 14 Figure 3: Elevations proffered with 21-01-REZ Figure 4: Proposed Elevations Following the deferral, staff provided the applicant with suggested modifications to the residential elevations to better align the submittal with the original proffers. The applicant has since submitted revisions that include some of the requested modifications (See Figure 4). Revisions to the elevations include adding side projections to Plan A with additional windows, reversing the porch roof orientation on Plan A, and adding roof brackets. However, the applicant declined to make some of staff’s requested modifications and can speak to these items during the meeting. These include providing a more recessed middle unit along the front and rear elevations, providing enhanced siding materials, and incorporating a more detailed architectural feature within the gable. Separate from the residential units, the three proposed commercial buildings will be reviewed individually through the Pattern Book approval process at the time of building permit application. This process is intended to ensure that future commercial development remains consistent with the overall architectural character and design standards established for The Depot at Fighting Creek, applicable ordinance requirements, and the approved rezoning proffers. 3|Page 15 Design Evaluation Pattern Book approval from the Planning Commission is required prior to building permit submittal for this project.
